subtype: Approach: adopts a topper's study schedule [Pitfall]
passage: In Class 10, I tried to become Trisha. I'm Lokesh. Trisha topped our school every year, and in an interview for the school magazine she said she woke at five and studied maths before sunrise. So I set my alarm for five. The trouble is, I've always been a night person. My brain wakes up around nine at night. For three weeks I dragged myself up at five, stared at equations with heavy eyes, and fell asleep in the second period. The teacher caught me twice. My maths test score dropped from 68 to 55. Papa found me asleep at the dining table one morning and said, "Beta, that's her routine, not yours." He was right. It fit her. It didn't fit me.

qa.q: What did Lokesh's maths score drop to?
How did Lokesh feel during the three weeks of five-am alarms?
qa.a: Lokesh felt exhausted and discouraged, dragging up with heavy eyes and falling asleep in class.

qa.q: What would suit Lokesh better than copying Trisha?
qa.a: Studying maths at night, when Lokesh's brain wakes up, and keeping mornings lighter.

qa.q: How might Trisha see her routine being copied?
qa.a: Trisha might be surprised, and would probably say it's what works for her, not a rule for everyone.

grounding: A teenager copies a topper's five-am routine though he is a night person, and ends up sleepy in class with poorer marks.

subtype: Approach: adopts a topper's study schedule [Pitfall]

Class teacher's note: Kiran, Class 9, unit test review

Kiran's marks have dropped in three subjects this month. He has been falling asleep in the first two periods. When I asked him, he told me he started waking at 4:45 to study, because Francis, our class topper, does that. Kiran said, "If it works for him, it should work for me." But he also said he's never been able to sleep before midnight, and that his best studying used to be at night. So he's now getting about five hours of sleep. I spoke to his parents and suggested he go back to his own evening routine. Francis's timetable fits Francis. We will check his energy and marks again in three weeks.

qa.q: What time did Kiran start waking to study?
Why did Kiran think Francis's routine would work for him?
qa.a: He felt hopeful that copying the topper would make him a topper, without thinking about his own sleep pattern.

qa.q: What would you advise Kiran now?
qa.a: Return to studying in the evening, when he works best, and get enough sleep, as the teacher suggested.

qa.q: How might Kiran's parents see the problem?
qa.a: His parents may feel worried about his sleep and relieved to have a clear, simple fix.

grounding: A teenager copies a topper's early routine though he is a night person, and becomes sleepy with poorer marks.
